rules: A row whose office the person already holds on a verse that says it is covered: the original reading held it only because the saying verse lay outside the chapter it was given, or it repeats the office from another verse.

A list the text heads or closes with a headship ('heads of fathers', 'princes in their families', 'ruled over the house of their father') says it of each man the list names, never of a forebear named in his chain or of a father named after 'sons of'.
'X son of Y, the <title>' gives the title to X at the head of the chain (Shallum, Maaseiah, Shechem).
A servant's standing (עֶבֶד, נַעַר, שִׁפְחָה, παιδίσκη) is not an occupation; the attendant's verb שֵׁרֵת said of a named person is (Joshua, Elisha, Abishag).
Leading men (רָאשִׁים, ἡγούμενοι) of a company, a procession or a church are a standing, not an office, unless a house or people is said they head.
A heavenly being's rule is a heavenly role (owner, 2026-10-27, TSK-1254).
Identity is the records' question: where a row turns on whether two names are one person, the occupation follows the record the verse's word is annotated to.

Gen 10:10 'the beginning of his kingdom (מַמְלַכְתּוֹ) was Babel': a man whose kingdom the text names is its king, as a verb of reigning counts.

1 Kgs 11:24-25: his band 'reigned in Damascus' and 'he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon... and reigned over Aram' (KJV, BSB 'Rezon... ruled over Aram'). The verb of reigning said of him.
